ai.description: This slender lizard reaches 20 cm total length. It is pale brown or sandy with dark reticulated patterns and possesses distinctive, comb-like fringes on its toes for navigating loose desert sand.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Acanthodactylus cantoris* is best distinguished by the distinct, comb-like serrated fringes on its toes, which are significantly more pronounced than in other Indian lacertids.
ai.habitat: *Acanthodactylus cantoris* inhabits arid, sandy plains and semi-desert regions of the Indian subcontinent, typically found in areas with sparse, xerophytic scrub vegetation.
ai.behavior: The Indian Fringe-fingered Lizard is a diurnal forager that uses its specialized, comb-like toe fringes to sprint rapidly across loose desert sands while hunting insects.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Acanthodactylus cantoris* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of 3–6 eggs. Breeding occurs primarily from April to July during the warmer months in India.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Acanthodactylus cantoris* inhabits the sandy deserts and arid plains of northwestern India, primarily across Rajasthan, Gujarat, Haryana, and Punjab at low elevations.
